comment: Review findings. Four independent reviews of codex/ui-audit-pass, each
given the spec and the diff and never another reviewer's reasoning.
verdict is provenance, not severity. 'reported' means a reviewer claimed
it and nobody has re-derived it here yet — a claim from a delegated agent
is a lead. 'confirmed' means it was reproduced in this repo, and the
evidence field carries the numbers or the code read that did it.
falsified is 1 only when the guard was made to FAIL against the restored
defect. A fix with falsified 0 is a fix nobody has proved is load-bearing.
fixed_in cannot be written by the commit that does the fixing: the hash does
not exist yet. Two gates then force the whole record to move together —
status fixed requires a real fixed_in, and falsified 1 requires status fixed.
So the FIXING commit leaves all three alone, and the NEXT commit sets status,
fixed_in and falsified in one go. Both halves of that were got wrong here and
the suite refused each in turn, which is the gates working as intended.
The two earlier reviews (browser, lib) are recorded at the granularity
that survived the session; their per-finding detail is in the transcript,
not here. Findings raised after this file existed are recorded whole.

findings.claim: Damage facts are built from @smogon/calc's fixed 3-hit pin while the engine rolls 2-5, so min/max/critMax/possibleKO/guaranteedKO all describe a move the game does not play.
findings.evidence: Probed: Icicle Spear, Rock Blast, Bullet Seed, Tail Slap all report calc .hits === 3. Cloyster Icicle Spear vs 250 HP Blissey read max=198 critMax=297 possibleKO=false; five hits deal 330 and five crits 495. Against 160 HP it read guaranteedKO=true, which two max-roll hits miss 35% of the time. After the fix: max=330 critMax=495 possibleKO=true, guaranteedKO=false.

findings.claim: Slush Rush is given hail immunity it does not have in Gen 8, so a hail attrition line predicts zero chip per turn where the game deals 1/16.
findings.evidence: Read the block directly. Root cause was ours: docs/CONSTANTS-AUDIT.md D11 read 'Ice Body/Snow Cloak/Slush Rush take no hail chip'. Hail is not symmetric with sand — sand exempts all three of its abilities, hail exempts only Ice Body and Snow Cloak. This repo's own ai/src/abilities.ts and ai/src/order.ts only ever gave Slush Rush a speed effect. Audit entry corrected rather than silently edited.

findings.claim: There are two disjoint representations of 'this was a crit'. A sampled crit sets criticalHitTargets but never fires Anger Point; a guaranteed crit fires Anger Point but never appears in the log.
findings.evidence: Probed. Machamp Tackle vs Anger Point Tauros, crit sampled: criticalHitTargets=["player-1"], boosts=undefined. Storm Throw (always-crit): criticalHitTargets=undefined, boosts={"player-1":{"atk":6}}. The 1/16 event Anger Point exists for cannot trigger it. Fixed in 0ff6e6a. Both paths now record into criticalHitTargets and Anger Point reads the resolved answer per target, so a spread move can crit one side only. The facts stay as a fallback for callers that supply damage directly instead of sampling.

findings.claim: criticalByTarget is one boolean per target, so a single crit draw applies to every hit of a multi-hit move. Mainline rolls the crit per hit.
findings.evidence: Probed Rock Blast: crit forced gives all hits identical, no-crit gives all hits identical — never mixed. Real 5-hit P(at least one crit) is 27.6% spread across 1-5 crit hits; this engine gives 6.25% all-five and 93.75% none. The mean survives, the distribution does not. Fixed in 0ff6e6a. Measured after: 30.1% of five-hit Rock Blasts crit over 627 samples against a theoretical 27.6% (1.4 standard errors), with zero all-five crits. The test classifies hits by damage band — ordinary 37-44, crit 56-66, disjoint — because an earlier version counted distinct damage values, which vary from ordinary roll spread regardless, and stayed green when hit 0's flag was applied to all five.

findings.claim: Moving the sleep counter onto the attempt made statusTurns === 0 unreachable, but three legality gates still test it, so Sleep Talk and Snore execute on the turn the user wakes.
findings.evidence: Probed at statusTurns=1. Sleep Talk: hit=true, notes 'actor woke on the attempt and acted' then 'Sleep Talk selected Tackle'. Snore: 19 damage. Mainline wakes the Pokemon and it does nothing. Gates at move-engine.ts:3106, actions.ts:594, call-legality.ts:42. Fixed in 16f664c. The rule now lives in ai/src/sleep.ts so the three gates cannot drift apart again. An undefined counter still counts as asleep, matching the old behaviour, rather than inventing a wake for hand-built states.

findings.claim: The held-item flinch never calls blocksSecondaryEffects and gates on total damage rather than direct damage, so it flinches through Shield Dust and through a Substitute.
findings.evidence: Probed Machamp + King's Rock Tackle at roll 0.05: flinch applied vs Shield Dust, vs Substitute, and vs the bare control alike. The move's OWN flinch secondary is correctly blocked in both cases, so only the item path is wrong. sequentialDamageOutcome(...).directDamage is computed 20 lines below and is the value it should gate on. Fixed in 16f664c by reusing effectTargetIds — the set the engine already computes for who receives a move's added effects, and where the Substitute filter lives (move-engine.ts:3528). canApplyVolatile does NOT check Substitute or Shield Dust; probed directly, it returns true for both. Shield Dust comes from blocksSecondaryEffects, the same call the secondary path makes.

findings.claim: The diff cites onBeforeMovePriority to move confusion above paralysis but leaves paralysis above infatuation, which the same ordering forbids. Reported marginals: mainline 33.0/33.5/8.4, this engine 33.0/25.1/16.75.
Showdown's Rainbow condition explicitly skips the doubling for a Serene Grace flinch secondary, so the x4 is wrong for the exact example the comment cites. 60% is correct there.

On the hitRolls branch pickRoll is called without the critical argument, so a rolled crit never reaches the damage — but criticalHitTargets and the trace note are set anyway. The announced crit deals less than the ordinary hit.
critBlocked checks the defender's ability but never calls ignoresTargetAbility, so a Mold Breaker attacker never crits a Battle Armor or Shell Armor target.

The mechanics wave added three draw sites, removed one and reordered two, but seed-keyed receipts record only schemaVersion. Every receipt written before the change now replays to different outcomes with no signal.
findings.evidence: Widened by 0ff6e6a: a variable multi-hit now draws N crits instead of 1, so seeded replay of any multi-hit move diverges from receipts written before it. Still only schemaVersion is checked.

findings.claim: Mainline runs sleep above truant and flinch, so the counter burns even on a flinched turn. Here both return first, so a flinched sleeper sleeps one turn longer. The recharge case is correct.

getEffectiveMoveMetadata returns defaults.multiHitRange unconditionally, and resolution puts hitCountOverride ahead of targetFacts.hits, so an explicit MoveState hits is honoured by the calculator then overwritten. Not currently reachable.
status.ts keeps a second crit list that folds in the always-crit four, so the Focus Energy policy believes it helps a Wicked Blow. Two hand-maintained copies of the same list is a drift hazard.
decrementSleep is now a no-op shim. Either the bookkeeping its comment mentions is real and should be named, or the function and its call site should go.

assert.equal(entry.chance, recomputed && entry.chance) evaluates to entry.chance whenever the recomputed value is non-zero, so the assertion compares a value to itself and the recomputed number is discarded.
findings.evidence: Read the source. Auditor also shifted the real quote by -5% and by hardcoding the catch rate to 255, both green. The fixture is Poochyena, whose rate IS 255, so the test cannot tell 'reads the rate' from 'hardcodes it' — and the test hardcodes it too. FIXED. The `X && entry.chance` tautology is gone and the quote is compared to a recomputed value from the ORACLE's rate rather than a hardcoded 255 — Poochyena's own rate, which is why the test could not tell 'reads the rate' from 'hardcodes it'. A second species discriminates: Abra at 200, NOT Ralts at 235, because the quote rounds to whole percent and 235 and 255 both land on 34%. Falsified: shift the quote -5% -> RED; hardcode 255 -> RED.

findings.claim: The test's own 'the race was actually staged' assertion only proves a DOM button exists. Making a move click send no request at all — race physically impossible — still passes. Either guard can also be deleted alone and it stays green.
findings.evidence: Auditor's mutation: guard the move click with an early return so no /run/battle/act request is issued. 1/1 pass. Fix is to count requests through page.route rather than assert a node exists. FIXED in 3df343c. Three defects: the anti-vacuity check was !!cleared (a DOM node exists), the outcome was three hardcoded V8 phrases, and it was the one test in the file with no skip guard. The route handler now counts turns; session.errors replaces the phrase matching. The partial-regression blind spot needed two NEW scenarios, because in the original race the request succeeds so both guards run and either suffices: one opens a second fight under the in-flight turn (isolating the success guard, discriminated by the battle LOG since both fights share a trainer and the opponent name is identical either way), one aborts the request (isolating the catch guard). Falsified: no request -> RED; success guard -> RED; catch guard -> RED; both -> RED.

findings.claim: The test claims the suspect-clock flag is part of the hash chain from birth, but deleting it from eventHashInput keeps the test green, because the hash is computed the same wrong way at write and at validate.
findings.evidence: Read eventHashInput: it deletes only id and eventHash, so production IS correct and the flag is covered. This is a test gap, not a production bug. Closing it means tampering with a bundle and expecting CORRUPT_EVENT. FIXED. Round-tripping proved nothing because the hash is computed the same way at write and at validate. The test now STRIPS observedAtSuspect from an exported bundle, rechecksums it, and requires CORRUPT_EVENT. Falsified: delete the flag from eventHashInput -> RED.

findings.claim: The shelf test only ever passes the correct prior checksum, so weakening the guard to accept any truthy supersedes stays green. A caller shipping supersedes: 'x' would overwrite any archive.
findings.evidence: Read the guard: production correctly requires incoming.supersedes === priorMark. Test gap. Closing it means asserting a wrong checksum is rejected with ARCHIVE_CONFLICT. FIXED. The test only ever passed the CORRECT prior checksum, so weakening the guard to accept any truthy supersedes stayed green. It now asserts that naming the WRONG checksum is still an ARCHIVE_CONFLICT and that the original survives it. Falsified: `if (incoming.supersedes) return;` -> RED.

findings.claim: The test's comment says it pins the outspeed-KO exemption, but every cell in the fixture short-circuits before that branch, so deleting the exemption entirely keeps it green.
findings.evidence: Found independently before the audit returned. Measured on the fixture: every pairing has critKO=false, so the outspeed branch is never evaluated. Closed by testing pairingLethal directly as an exported function; that unit test goes red when the credit is removed.

findings.claim: answer.steps is empty for the fixture, so the forEach over it runs zero assertions. Unwiring the shared-bag ledger completely left 82/82 green.
findings.evidence: Fourth vacuous test found this session. Closed by extracting affordableOptions() and pinning the selection rule directly; restoring the unfunded fallback turns it red. The end-to-end count was left out on purpose and the test says so.

findings.claim: The focus-ring assertion is substring presence in a CSS file, so keeping the selector and deleting its outline declaration stays green. Sibling assertions on the same line use a real regex and do bite.
findings.evidence: FIXED. Substring presence replaced with a regex bounded to the rule's OWN braces. The first attempt used a {0,600} window and was still not a check: deleting the selector's outline let it match one from a later rule and stay green. Falsified: keep the selector, delete its outline -> RED.

findings.claim: The fix left both hand-rolled crit lists in place and the test reaches only the calc-adapter copy, so the original defect can be reintroduced in status.ts and stay green. Sky Attack and Snipe Shot are named in a comment but asserted nowhere.
findings.evidence: FIXED. HIGH_CRIT_MOVES and ALWAYS_CRIT_MOVES are exported from calc-adapter and imported by status.ts, so there is one list rather than two hand-kept copies. status.ts also stopped folding the always-crit four into the high-crit question, which had it believing Focus Energy helps a Wicked Blow. The gate asserts membership by name — 'Sky Attack and Snipe Shot are in the set too' had been prose, and deleting them stayed green — and asserts from SOURCE that status.ts imports rather than declares. My first identity check was itself a tautology: statusModule.HIGH_CRIT_MOVES ?? HIGH_CRIT_MOVES compared the fallback to itself. Falsified: corrupt the canonical list -> RED; delete skyattack/snipeshot -> RED; restore a local copy -> RED.

findings.claim: The Math.random guard covers only the ordinary-move advanceTurn call. Removing the rng from the forced-replacement site or the ball-throw site leaves the test green, and the fix repaired all three.
findings.evidence: FIXED. The seeded test drove only the ordinary-move advanceTurn; the ball-throw and held-end-of-turn calls were unguarded. It now drives all three under the same poisoned Math.random. The forced-replacement case needed the INCOMING mon to carry the Starf Berry — without it the held end-of-turn has nothing random to resolve, so stripping that rng changed nothing and the first version of the gate passed against the very mutation it existed to catch. Falsified: strip the rng at lines 699, 745 and 806 -> RED, independently.

findings.claim: 27 of 28 tests in the file carry a skip guard; the one added by this diff does not, so without Chromium it throws instead of skipping and breaks the file's stated contract.
When nothing affordable improved a Pokemon the selection fell back to the unfunded list, so one Focus Sash could be handed to three Pokemon and each was told it was now safe.
findings.evidence: Could not reproduce the reviewer's exact repro with a 3-mon party, but the rule was unsound on reading and pickups are never in the bag by construction, so affordableFromBag returns false for every pickup option. Fixed by removing the fallback outright.

findings.claim: pairingLethal credits 'we outspeed and KO on our worst roll' without checking whether their crit comes from a priority move. Mach Punch swings first no matter how fast we are.
findings.evidence: Priority moves appear in real exposure lists. Cells now carry critPriority from lib/planner.js and the credit is refused when set. The test goes red when critPriority is ignored.

findings.claim: archive() never named what it replaced and list() aborted the whole legacy import on the first conflict, despite an earlier commit message claiming both were wired.
findings.evidence: The edit was claimed in a commit message and was not in the file. Now wired, with legacy records imported one at a time so one conflict cannot lose the rest.

findings.claim: normalizeArchive stamped archivedAt from the wall clock, so the same run hashed differently on every archive and no content-addressed comparison could hold.
findings.evidence: archivedAt now derives from endedAt or startedAt, or is null.

findings.claim: 47 authored :hover rules were unguarded, so on a touch screen a tapped button keeps its hover background and reads as still-selected. The app is responsive to 640px and is held while playing.
findings.evidence: Counted through the CSSOM in a real browser, not by grepping source. Before: 35 bare hover rules live at 375x812 with pointer:coarse. After: 47 inert, 0 focus-visible trapped behind the guard, 30 remaining are vendor (bootstrap 28, select2 2) and deliberately out of scope. Desktop hover still works: border rgb(46,58,68) -> rgb(74,90,102).

findings.claim: The first pass of the hover codemod scoped itself to two stylesheets by assumption, so dark-theme.css kept 5 unguarded :hover rules while the new source gate reported green.
findings.evidence: Only a CSSOM count in a running browser found it — the source-level gate could not, because the gate and the codemod shared the same wrong file list. Worth remembering: a gate that reads the same scope as the fix cannot check the scope.

findings.claim: Nothing asserts that per-commit cost stays flat as the log grows. The wall-clock assertion that used to stand there was removed because it measured machine load, and no contention-proof replacement was found.
findings.evidence: Original gate: 11.5s under the full suite, 2.5s alone, identical code. A scaling ratio (second 5000 commits over the first) was tried and is also load-sensitive: 0.83-0.94 alone, 2.43 in suite. The loop IS flat — per-1000 blocks measured 88, 94, 67, 57, 49, 54, 65, 55, 61 ms — and an injected O(n) scan does show up at 2.57, but the healthy and loaded ranges overlap so the gate cannot separate them. Needs either a serialized perf lane or an operation counter rather than a clock. FIXED with the operation counter this finding asked for. The claim is algorithmic — a commit is O(1) in the length of the log — so it is counted rather than timed. Every scanning method on Array.prototype is wrapped for the duration of the loop and counts only when the receiver is already large, so a commit that appends and looks nothing up never triggers one while a commit that searches the log does, whichever internal array it searches. That matters because the store does not expose its state, and this needs no access to it. Measured 0 across 4000 commits, and 3501 with a single state.events.some(...) injected after the push: the healthy and regressed ranges no longer overlap, which is exactly what the wall clock and the scaling ratio could not manage. Restored in a finally, or every test after it runs against a patched Array. The same commit retired a SECOND clock gate that had been introduced hours earlier in tests/run.test.js — an absolute 3s budget on the C(30,6) enumeration, which read 585ms alone and 4829ms under the full suite beside this very test. Replaced by asserting combinations, which is exact and moves only when behaviour moves.

findings.claim: unusedRoutes only set `open` when availability.json had a date, so an undated location had no `open` property and every consumer's `route.open` filter dropped it. 18 of 69 route-units were excluded from every answer at every point in the run, 12 of them with walk encounters.
findings.evidence: Raised by Philip noticing the early towns list no encounters. availability.json's own `method` field says it dates a location by its first trainer, so trainerless places — Oldale Town, Littleroot Town, the whole Safari Zone, Fiery Path, Shoal Cave, Sky Pillar, Mirage Tower, Artisan Cave, Altering Cave, Sootopolis, Ever Grande — get no date. Measured on a fresh run: 4 of 69 offered, 18 dropped. Oldale Town has 7 walkable mons at levels 2-3 and run.apply({kind:'catch',map:'Oldale Town'}) is accepted, so the tables were always fine. Now flagged undated and counted out loud, following the undatedMovesExcluded pattern.

findings.claim: availability.json dates 83 of the oracle's 123 locations. The 40 undated ones are exactly those with no trainer standing in them, because the dating method anchors to a location's first trainer. They can now be reported as unknown but still cannot be planned around.
findings.evidence: Counted directly: 123 oracle locations, 83 dated entries, 40 undated. d2a77a9 makes the gap visible rather than silent, but does not close it. Hand-dating needs Philip's call — the file's provenance is 'transcribed', and only Littleroot Town (the starting town) and Oldale Town (walked through in the first minutes) look certain enough to assert without a source. CLOSED. The R&B tracker order dated 33 of the 40 in 8ffb2ee. Measured now: 7 undated of 123 locations, and all seven are content nothing can date — Artisan Cave and two Safari Zone corners the tracker never lists, plus three unused Cave of Origin maps and Safari Zone Northeast. Undated is now the honest answer for those rather than a gap.

findings.claim: Fishing is gated at order 0 and no rod is modelled, so every rod-only encounter is offered as 'Catchable now' from the very first fight — including locations whose ONLY current encounters are rod-gated.
findings.evidence: Walked the running app. Littleroot Town at fight 0 shows 'Catchable now - 4': Surskit, Lotad, Finneon, Tympole, all labelled Super Rod. Philip's account of the route is that the rod comes from Route 103, so at fight 0 none of those are catchable. availability.json methods reads {walk:0, fish:0, surf:589, rock-smash:139}; lib/run.js contains zero mentions of Old/Good/Super Rod and no rod gate. All 336 fish slots in the game are Super Rod, so one gate would cover every one of them. At fight 0 both Littleroot Town and Route103 offer ONLY rod-gated encounters as available now. Same shape as the Petalburg City defect: the tool offers work the player cannot do yet. Needs Philip's call on the order the rod becomes available before it can be fixed. REFUTED on closer reading, and the error was mine. Youngster Calvin — the fight at order 0 — stands on ROUTE 102 (rab-trainers-database.json gives him location 'Route 102'). Route 103, where Philip says the rod is, has minOrder 0 and is reachable BEFORE him: Oldale has two exits and both trackers order Route 103 ahead of Route 102. So by the first fight the rod is already obtainable, and fish:0 is correct. I asserted 'at fight 0 none of those are catchable' by assuming the player had not detoured north yet, which the canonical route contradicts. The UI also already labels every one of those slots 'Super Rod', so it is not hiding the requirement either. Left recorded rather than deleted: a refuted finding is evidence too, and the next reader should not re-raise it.

findings.claim: A gated encounter row printed the bare fight order beside the species — 'Squirtle L5 · 30% · #589' — which in a Pokemon app reads as a National Dex number.
findings.evidence: Philip reading the live app: 'it says: If you come back · 4 more from fight #589 but thats the pokemon #'. #589 is Escavalier. The order was never the useful fact; the row wants Surf. The heading now says it once in words and the row tooltip carries the number, worded as a fight. Falsified three ways including deleting the label entirely, which a pure absence check would have passed.

findings.claim: Each encounter row was a single concatenated string, so with proportional species names the level, method and odds began at a different x on every line. There were no fields to align.
findings.evidence: Measured in the browser: rows rendered as '<button>Surskit  L2-3  Super Rod  · 40%</button>' with one text node. After splitting into spans and gridding: one left edge per column across all eight rows (36/203/264/344). Two things only measurement caught — the per-row gate label widened a column on gated rows only, pushing level and odds 68px out of line, and a 1fr name column aligned correctly but sprawled the full 1040px.

findings.claim: Upstream's base .btn sets a fixed width: 5em. Run-panel labels are variable-length prose, so 'Undo last change' got 67px for 114px of text — wrapping to two lines, then overflowing 42px past the column once nowrap was added.
findings.evidence: Measured: box 67px, rendered text right edge 1109 against a container right edge of 1067. The calculator lives with the fixed width by opting into .btn-wide per button. Run-panel buttons now size to their label and cap at the container. A browser gate at 1280x900 and 375x812 now forbids overflow, clipped labels and sideways scroll.

findings.claim: runbun-run-plan-actions and runbun-run-advice carry a 1px border, so while empty they painted a 2px-tall bordered box that read as a broken divider.
findings.evidence: Measured 589x2 and 615x2 with zero children and no text, inside a 1042px column. Two more turned up once the gate existed: the encounter list and the history list.

findings.claim: The oracle models only WILD encounter tables. Gifts, in-game trades, Game Corner badge rewards and fossils are invisible, so guaranteed free Pokemon are never offered to a nuzlocke planner.
findings.evidence: Found via the tracker workbook's 'Other' and 'Game Corner' sheets while checking a starter question. Probed with scripts/ask.js: Kubfu (Mossdeep gift) NOT FINDABLE; Castform (Weather Institute gift) NOT FINDABLE; Growlithe-Hisui (Rustboro trade) NOT FINDABLE. The sheets list: 3 trades (Rustboro Growlithe-Hisui, Fortree Weezing-Galar, Pacifidlog Zorua-Hisui), 3 gifts (Lavaridge 'Egg with a random Hoenn starter', Weather Institute Castform, Mossdeep Kubfu), fossils at Rustboro, and 8 badge-gated Game Corner rewards up to 'Mew, Celebi, Jirachi or Victini' at the Rain Badge. For a run where every encounter is scarce these are the opposite of marginal. MERGED with non-wild-species-sources-missing, which the platform audit raised independently: 8 badge-gated Game Corner tiers (ending at 'Mew, Celebi, Jirachi or Victini' on the Rain Badge), 3 in-game trades, the Lavaridge starter egg, Castform, Kubfu and the fossils. Two audits reaching the same defect from different directions is corroboration, not two problems. FIXED. profiles/run-and-bun/oracle/sources.json now carries the 8 badge-gated Game Corner tiers with their options and odds, the 3 trades with what they cost, the gifts, the fossils and the 7 roaming legendaries. availabilityOfSpecies gained an obtainable status and reports EVERY route — Larvitar is both a Heat Badge reward and a wild, and an earlier version returned on the first wild table and dropped the guaranteed one. Timing that the source does not give is null rather than guessed: the roaming legendaries carry after-prose, and three gifts have no location on file.

findings.claim: The three starter choices are hardcoded in the page template and nowhere in the profile, so nothing can validate them and no tool can answer what the game starts you with.
findings.evidence: `node scripts/ask.js starters` reports 'NOT MODELLED'. Raised when Philip said R&B starts with Piplup, Chimchar and Turtwig. Three independent sources say the Hoenn trio instead: the tracker workbook's Other sheet lists a Lavaridge gift of 'Egg with a random Hoenn starter'; the rab trainer database gives May the ace Sceptile/Blaziken/Swampert across all 17 rival fights; and Piplup/Chimchar/Turtwig appear nowhere in the workbook. UNRESOLVED pending Philip — recorded because the disagreement is only possible at all because the data does not state the answer anywhere. RESOLVED by Philip: keep the rival data, fix the player's starter. Run & Bun rebuilt the player starter to the Sinnoh line while leaving the rival's teams hand-built around Hoenn, so the two lists are deliberately from different generations. STARTERS now lives in profiles/run-and-bun/encounters.js beside RIVAL_ACES, the page and lib/play.js both read it instead of holding copies, and a gate asserts the page offers exactly the profile's trio, that the visible label matches its own data-species, and that a well-meaning alignment of the two lists goes red.

findings.claim: The tool cannot distinguish 'this hack removed the species' from 'we do not model that source'. ask.js where Kubfu and ask.js where Caterpie both answer NOT FINDABLE, though one is a guaranteed free gift and the other can never be obtained.
findings.evidence: Measured. The hack's own Pokemon Locations.xlsx carries an 'Unavailable Pokemon' sheet naming ~416 species across 8 generation rows; none of it is modelled. For a nuzlocke planner these are the two most different answers possible — one is a Pokemon you are missing, the other is one to stop planning around. Plan: docs/MODELLING-GAPS.md phase 0. FIXED. The hack's own Unavailable list (416 named species across 8 generations, plus Generation IX wholesale) is now profile data, and availabilityOfSpecies returns five distinct answers: unavailable, not-modelled, wild, unreachable, contested. Cross-checking the list against the ROM-derived wild tables found 8 contradictions; 6 are explained by their only source standing in content nothing can date (Safari Zone SE/NE, Artisan Cave), and 2 — Geodude in Magma Hideout, Duraludon in Shoal Cave — are a genuine disagreement recorded as contested rather than resolved silently.

findings.claim: lib/run.js charges Rare Candy for over-cap levels and a Heart Scale for relearner moves, but neither appears among the 28 modelled field items, so the tool spends currencies it cannot tell you how to earn.
findings.evidence: Measured: 28 field items modelled against 127 location references across the six sheets of Item Locations.xlsx, whose first sheet is 'Heart Scale Location'. Every evolution stone is missing too — Fire, Water, Thunder, Moon, Sun, Dusk — which is the input evolution planning needs most. Plan: docs/MODELLING-GAPS.md phase 2. FIXED, and the data turned out to be already here. item-workbook.json holds 30 Heart Scale locations and 14 Rare Candy, each with a place and a hiding spot, and no code read it — the same shape lib/item-facts was in before it got a consumer. oracle.currencySources(name) exposes them and both refusals now end with the sources: levelUp adds 13 known sources: Route 110, Route 116, Mauville City, and 10 more; heartScale adds 19 known sources: Route 104, Route 106, Route 118, and 16 more. PLACES, NOT DATES, deliberately. 27 of the 30 Heart Scale rows and 9 of the 14 Rare Candy rows do join a dated map, so dating them looks easy, and it is the same inference moveObtainableAt refuses for TMs — a location string with no gating clause is not evidence that no gate exists. Where was the whole of what the refusal was missing; when is a separate question with a separate standard of proof and it is Philip to answer. The evolution stones stay out for a different reason rather than the same one: their sheet stores prose in the place column, Sold at Mauville City Pokemon Mart and the like, so 0 of 23 join anything and a list built from it would be a sentence pretending to be a place. That half of the claim — every evolution stone missing, which is the input evolution planning needs most — is NOT closed by this and is worth its own entry. Gate in tests/run.test.js made to fail four ways: silence the clause, drop it from either refusal alone, and drop the command prefix, which matters because run-api keys its 400s on it and losing it turns a refusal into a 500. REOPENED, by its own probe and correctly. scripts/recheck-findings.js checks whether Rare Candy and Heart Scale appear among availability.json items, and they still do not: fieldItems models 28 and neither currency is among them, so a player asking what there is to pick up still cannot see either. What f47bc3c fixed is the second half of the claim — the tool can now tell you how to earn what it spends, because both refusals end with the places from the workbook. What it did not touch is the first half, that the items are absent from the map the rest of the tool reads. Marking it fixed was over-claiming, and the recheck gate caught it in the same run. The probe is left exactly as it was rather than narrowed to match what was built: a probe rewritten to agree with the change is not a probe. What remains is an import — put the workbook rows on the item map with places and no dates, the same standard the refusal text already uses — and it is worth doing beside evolution-stones-have-prose-where-a-place-should-be, which is the same shelf.

findings.claim: The evolution-item sheet stores prose where every other sheet stores a place, so none of its 23 rows can be joined to a map and evolution planning has no source list at all.

findings.claim: The fair-dice survival sampler does not scale Reversal, Flail or Endeavor with the user's missing health, so an enemy that holds a sash or pinch berry with one of those moves is forecast as a scratch and plays as a sweep. 41 fights in the run map carry the set.
findings.evidence: Found by the calibration curve, not by anyone reading code: win rate by predicted losses ran 100 / 81.5 / 98.2 / 100 down the buckets, and a verdict predicting ONE loss losing more often than one predicting three is a bucket that means something other than what it says. Every loss in that bucket was Battle Girl Lilith: 12 of 14 attempts, each forecast "decided by 9 · a sampled branch loses 1 Pokemon". The transcript shows why — her Mankey holds Focus Sash + Reversal, survives our best hit at 2%, and one-shots six consecutive slower switch-ins with max-power STAB Reversal before any of them moves. Predicted 1, actual 7. The blindness is structural: the pinned provider bundle contains the string Reversal exactly once, as a move-table name, with no HP-threshold power formula anywhere, while the engine that PLAYS the fight implements the scaling (calc gen789, case Reversal) — which is why the played sweep is real and the sampled scratch is not. Sized against the run map: 51 threshold movers, 41 anchored by sash, pinch berry, Sturdy or Endure, from Fisherman Darian's Flail Magikarp at order 14 to Reversal Urshifu and Crabominable on two Elite Four teams. Over the post-perf batch, 23 of 30 threshold fights lost two or more MORE than predicted (loss_mae 2.6 overall), and excluding them repairs the whole curve: the loses-1 bucket goes 81.5% to 100.0% and both monotonicity breaks vanish. MITIGATED in 11519d9: planNext returns thresholdThreats and the verdict appends a CAUTION naming the set — an unanchored threshold mover is deliberately not named, so the warning stays rare enough to read. NOT FIXED here, because the sampler is the pinned vendor provider and re-pinning it is the other session's surface; the fix is Reversal/Flail/Endeavor power scaling in the provider, and this entry plus tags.underpriced = true in MLflow is the acceptance test waiting for it. Every mispriced fight carries a trace with the transcript as events and an expectation/feedback pair, QC-verified complete (455 traces, 7,765 turn spans, 17,061 events). CORRECTED 2026-08-26, same day: the actual-loss counts above were inflated by my own instrument. Faint lines carry no side prefix — Makuhita fainted! is the enemy and Pidgeotto fainted! is ours — and the first counter tallied both sides, which is how a six-slot party recorded seven deaths. Recounted against the timeline names: Lilith is predicted 1, lost 6 (the whole party), and threshold fights underpriced by 2+ drop from 23 to 12 of 30. Every win-rate figure and the calibration split stand unchanged, because they never used the faint count. The severity direction is unchanged too — a forecast of one loss against a full wipe. PLAY-LEVEL MITIGATION MEASURED, 2026-08-26, revision 20d4c01, two valid interleaved batches, 24 runs: threshold fights went 42 won, 0 lost, against 18 won 12 lost on the prior revision. The transcripts show the counter-line executing — Low Sweep into the sash holder, one trade at most, then the slowed 1-HP survivor is collected by whoever moves first — which is the speed-control fix (damaging drops playable, lethal clause removed), shared by both arms. The threshold-prep TEACH hook itself measured nothing at reach level: pooled n=12 per arm, Gavi 7/12 in both, Brawly 0/12 control vs 2/12 treatment at p=0.24, and the direction flipped between batches, which is the repository-documented under-15 pattern. Kept as cheap insurance — it fires only when the party lacks a priority attack and taught twice across twelve treatment runs. The SAMPLER blindness this entry is about still stands: verdicts on these fights still read loses-1, they are simply no longer true the expensive way. ISOLATED, 2026-08-26, batch spdctl: speed control as its own flag, control arm restoring the old policy exactly (pure-status drops only, lethal turns refused — gated both directions before the batch ran). Fight-level, where the feature aims: the control lost 2 of 6 Lilith attempts while treatment lost 0 of 8 threshold fights, and pooled across every run carrying the feature it is now 50 threshold fights, 0 losses, against 12W-2L in the same-revision control and 18W-12L on the pre-fix revision. Run-level, honestly: the control came out AHEAD this batch (meanOrder 75.8 vs 57.2, Gavi 4/6 vs 2/6) — the third consecutive batch whose run-level direction flipped, on a metric Gavi dominates and Gavi is measured box luck (Flame Wheel 1.4x per win, 0x per loss). The run-level claim stays unproven at n=6 per arm; the fight-level claim is the one the feature makes, and it holds under isolation. Default stays on.

findings.claim: Reflect, Light Screen and Aurora Veil have no row in the 78-source TM and tutor table — not undated, absent — so the advisor can never offer a screen and every screen play-rule in the driver is unreachable.
findings.evidence: Found by a mechanism check that saved a false conclusion. The screen rule was given the same lost-race lethal exception that fixed status moves and speed drops (gated, falsified three ways), and A/B batch scrctl came back with the strongest tallies of the session: control 0 of 6 past Gavi and 0 of 72 attempts, treatment 3 of 6, one Brawly win, and a run reaching order 162 — the deepest of the whole session — at p 0.05 to 0.09. Counting actual presses refuted the credit: screens were pressed ZERO times in BOTH arms across all twelve runs, so the treatment was inert and the split is box luck wearing a p-value. The cause chain, each link verified: moveObtainableAt answers null for both screens; the advisor correctly refuses undated teaches; and the moveItems table holds no row for any of the three at all, so this is a missing source rather than a missing date. No common early box species learns a screen by level-up at 21 either — a scan of 22 recorded box species found zero — which is why the n=1 Brawly win that used Reflect was an outlier catch rather than a repeatable line. What unblocks it: source the screen TMs (where does Run & Bun hand out TM33/TM16 or their equivalents), date them if the location text carries no gate, and the already-shipped play rule activates on its own. The scrctl batch is preserved in MLflow (labels scrctl-A/B, QC PASS) as the measured record of an inert treatment producing a p=0.05 tally — the standing example of why the mechanism check is part of the review standard. TEST CASE RULED BY PHILIP, 2026-08-26: Orbeetle learns both screens before Brawly, so a pinned box holding it is the activation test — no TM sourcing needed first. Verified in this tree: the whole Blipbug line is in the encounter tables, Dottler learns Reflect by level-up at 10, and Orbeetle knows both screens from level 1. Dottler was a recorded LOSS lead at Camper Gavi twelve times in the post-perf batch, so the boxes have been carrying a screen learner all along; the advisor taught Reflect exactly once. The pinned-box experiment is the next step when screens come back up, and the rule it would exercise is already shipped and gated behind --screen-control. ACTIVATED AND MEASURED, 2026-08-27, batch scrpin3: the full chain ran — pinned Blipbug line, fillToolSlots teaching Reflect and Light Screen into Dottler free slots, twelve clean runs, no disk aborts. Dottler was fielded in all 144 Camper Gavi fights; the control pressed zero screens and the treatment pressed 107, which is the first fully-verified mechanism execution of the whole thread. The outcome is a REAL null: 0 of 72 Gavi attempts won in both arms, identical stalls at orders 34-48. On this box, at this wall, screens change nothing — the seven-species pin was chosen for catch reliability, not strength, and is simply too weak for Gavi with or without screens. What this does NOT measure is screens at Brawly, the all-physical wall the n=1 win credited them for, because no pinned run reached him. The next experiment needs a Gavi-viable pin, and the box composition is a game-knowledge choice. MEASURED AT ALL THREE GYMS, 2026-08-28, battery gymcf2: the counterfactual generator taught Reflect and Light Screen to the party LEAD of banked gym-adjacent boxes (the first cut taught the last two bodies in party order and measured zero because every screen arrived after four deaths — order verified before crediting). Full mechanism chain confirmed: screens on the lead bar, pressed exactly twice per fight in 30 of 30 probed fights per gym, and the engine models the halving (Zen Headbutt 59% into Qwilfish without Reflect, 28% with, same seed). Outcome: 0/30, 0/30, 0/30 at Brawly, Roxanne, Wattson — identical to baseline — and stacking screens+slow ONTO max IVs scored WORSE than max IVs alone (Roxanne 1 vs 7, Wattson 1 vs 15), because a line move replaces a damage move and the attack-turn tax exceeds the mitigation at a wall. Max IVs alone moved Roxanne 0->7/30 and Wattson 1->15/30 (Brawly 0/30 even at 31s). The gym walls are stats, quantified; sourcing the screen TMs remains a data gap but no longer carries a measured win hypothesis at any wall tested. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED high->medium 2026-08-28: gymcf2 measured screens at zero effect on every tested wall with the full mechanism chain verified, so no win hypothesis rests on sourcing these TMs any more — the row is a data-completeness gap, not a blocker.

findings.claim: Every number the panel shows beside a trainer — "(#77)" on verdicts, rank notes, the board and the next-fight line — is the cumulative-Pokemon order, not the trainer count a player thinks in. The converter exists and no display surface uses it.
findings.evidence: Raised by Philip, who had asked for this before and found the surfaces unchanged — the request predates this session's context and the machinery half-answers it: trainerIndexOf(run, order) exists, docs/RUN_API.md states the reason in one line ("order counts cumulative enemy POKEMON. A player counts TRAINERS"), and the two-order-scales confusion is a recorded recurring hazard (Brawly is engine row 28, run-map order 77, and only availability.json catches a crossed scale). Display sites found: run_panel.js 838 (next-fight line), 2344 (rank note), 2433 (advice note), 2565 (board title), 2849 (playbook title) — plus every driver journal line and report that echoes them. The change is display-plumbing, not arithmetic, but it has a deliberate blast radius: several browser and CLI gates pin the "(#0)" format (browser_run, play.test), so each must move with the format in the same commit rather than being loosened. The internal identifiers — position, opensAt anchors, caps — stay on the order scale, which is load-bearing; this finding is about what a PLAYER is shown beside a name. FIXED in the named commit: all five panel sites and eight CLI lines read fightNumber, every payload carries it beside order (which stays load-bearing for caps and anchors), and trainerIndexOf was made ABSOLUTE over the visible map — the old implementation walked the unbeaten road, so Brawly was the 26th trainer at run start and the 6th by the time you reached him, and the skip reordering would have bent it further. Falsified by the eleven format gates themselves: they were moved by VALUE (Calvin #0 to #1, Brawly #77 to #26) and the suite fails on any surface still printing the order — the straggler at play.js adjudicate was caught exactly that way in the same run.

findings.claim: When a level-up brings a pending move, teachPending replaces options[0] — whatever happens to sit first in the replace select — so a levelling Pokemon can blindly overwrite a real attack with a status move, and the advisor then spends a later round buying the slot back.
findings.evidence: Found while answering whether the taught-but-never-pressed Attack drops were advisor picks. They were not: 48 of 48 journal-attributable teaches of Charm, Baby-Doll Eyes and Feather Dance came from level-up prompts, zero from the advisor, and 72 of 85 were overwritten again by later teaches — only 13 survived to run end. The churn pair that exposes the mechanism is Spheal: "learned Charm over Ice Ball" 27 times across the batches, then "Brine over Charm" 27 times — the level-up prompt ate Ice Ball because it was FIRST IN THE SELECT, not because it was worth least, and the advisor later paid a round to restore a Water attack. teachPending picks options[0] as the replace target; the driver already owns a priced answer (moveValue) and uses it nowhere in this path. The cost is bounded — level-up teaches are free and the advisor does reclaim slots — but every reclaim is an advise round spent undoing a blind choice, and a party can walk into a fight between the two states. Fix shape: replace the least valuable current move by moveValue instead of options[0], which is one line plus a gate. Philip also notes stat-drop moves can be deliberately kept to create advantages for OTHER party members — a support-role line the driver does not yet have — so a smarter replace choice should undervalue a drop the play rules can now actually press, rather than auto-purging it.

findings.claim: Worst-case planning names the hardest SINGLE hit and whether a crit kills, but says nothing about an attrition race. A full nuzlocke wiped to repeated fixed-damage chip while the readiness strip read 'No crit kills anyone'.
findings.evidence: Played a complete nuzlocke in the browser. Won 5 fights (Calvin, Rick, Allen, Tiana, Mikey; position 0->9), then wiped: all four survivors died to Triathlete Mikey's Sonic Boom. Measured: Sonic Boom is fixed 20 damage, rolls=[20], min=max=20, every roll identical — no crit and no variance, so possibleKO and guaranteedKO both read false against a 34 HP target it two-shots. The switch logic fired four times, each triggered by the panel's own 'a crit KOs you' line, each into a 100% body, and every switch merely fed the next Pokemon in to be two-shotted. Against a fixed-damage attacker a switch is not a mitigation, and the tool's advice pointed at one. The ceiling verdict is sound; the missing question is 'can I out-race 20 a turn'. REPLAYED from the stored battle.ended event, which carries seed 435922576, 17 turns, outcome lost, and the full 20-action sequence: Tackle, Tackle, switch, Tackle, Tackle, switch, Leafage, Leafage, switch, Bubble x5, switch, Tackle, switch, Leafage, switch, Tackle. Six switches into a Yanma using Sonic Boom, and all four deaths recorded as by:'Sonic Boom' of:'Yanma'. The capture is good; the advice that produced those six switches is the defect. FIXED in 3b9f53e. incomingThreat now returns a race: turnsToKill against turnsToDie, pessimal on both sides, ties broken by Speed, and cannot-win when nothing we hold damages it. Verified live: "you need 2 turns to KO, they need 4 — you win it".

findings.claim: The tool plans and fights at the level cap but never lists getting there as work. preFightOpportunities returns before/encounters/items/moves and mentions levelling nowhere, so the grind between a catch and the party being planned with is invisible.
findings.evidence: Philip caught it reading a completed test run: 'we didn't level did we...'. Correct — the run had no levelUp command at all, and the box finished at catch levels (Turtwig L5, Lillipup L2, Gossifleur L2, Surskit L2). The battle driver still fought at 'Turtwig L12 · at cap' because it projects to the next milestone (Team Aqua Grunt Petalburg Woods, ace Croagunk, cap 12), so the simulation was fair. But the gap between stored and projected is real work the tool never names: Turtwig 7 levels, Gossifleur 10. In a nuzlocke that is hours of grinding, and preFightOpportunities — the literal 'before this fight' list — has no level key. The projection is right; the silence about how to reach it is not. FIXED. preFightOpportunities returns a levels key: the cap the NEXT fight is planned at, which fight sets it and with what ace, every party member below it with the levels each owes, and the total. On the run this finding was raised from it reads 4 of 4 below the cap of 12, 37 levels between them, set by Team Aqua Grunt Petalburg Woods and Croagunk, Turtwig L5 to L12 and three L2s to L12. The panel lists it first, because it is the only row there that is work already owned rather than something to go and find, and it carries no action button because kind drives a reveal-and-scroll and there is no section to send anyone to. Two decisions asserted rather than assumed: the cap comes from capAt(run, next.order) instead of the run cap, since the two differ exactly when the next fight is the one that raises it; and a Pokemon ABOVE the cap owes nothing, because the projection raises and never lowers, so counting it would turn a finished party into a to-do list. An at-cap party still reports the key rather than omitting it, since an absent key reads as not-modelled. Gate in tests/run.test.js made to fail three ways: never populating it, reading a cap the fight does not set, and counting over-cap members as work owed. One falsification found a rule rather than a bug — levelling the fixture past the cap was refused for want of a Rare Candy per level, which is engine-debits-currencies-it-cannot-source guarding itself, and the fixture now funds it.

findings.claim: The levelUp command raises the level and leaves the moveset untouched, so a Pokemon levelled from 5 to 12 permanently knows only its level-5 moves. Philip: 'We are not fighting with the right movesets because we're not actually leveling the Pokemon. We're just inflating the level to the cap.'
findings.evidence: Measured: catch Chimchar at L5 (Scratch, Leer, Ember), levelUp to cap -> L12 with the SAME three moves. Its real learnset gives Mach Punch at L10. Every fight after any level-up was fought with a moveset the Pokemon would not have. Fixed so a free slot fills automatically — which is what the game does without asking — while a full moveset is reported for a deliberate teach rather than guessed at, because the game stops and asks which move to forget.

findings.claim: partySpecs projects a party to the cap of the fight being planned but copies moves verbatim from the box, so every matchup, plan and safety answer was computed against a moveset the player would not have at that level.
findings.evidence: Read at lib/run.js:1084 — level was Math.max(mon.level, projected) while moves was mon.moves. Confirmed live in the UI: Chimchar shown as 'L12 - at cap' offering only Scratch, Ember and Leer. The same projectMoves helper now backs both projection and the real levelUp, so the two cannot drift apart.

findings.claim: The ledger's commit gate asserts fixed_in is an ancestor of HEAD. It does not assert the named commit CONTAINS the fix, so a finding can point at a commit that has nothing to do with it and stay green.
findings.evidence: Happened here. A shell && chain broke on a gitignored path, so two code fixes landed inside a LEDGER commit while findings.json pointed at the ledger commit BEFORE it (a7cd070) — which contains only findings.json. Both findings read as fixed, the gate passed, and the SHA was unrelated to the change. This is the same shape as the defect the gate was built for: a commit message claiming an edit it does not carry. A stronger gate would check that the named commit touches at least one file the finding names, which is cheap since findings already carry a file path.

findings.claim: The pinned pokemon-mono provider carries VANILLA abilities while this fork's calc data carries Run & Bun's. 97 of the 436 catchable wild species the provider knows (22%) have an ability it refuses, so catching one of them silently kills the fair-dice forecast for every fight while it is in the party — the outlook block hides itself and the recommended lead disappears.
findings.evidence: Found by scripts/ui-playthrough.js: the Plan panel showed only AI action scores, never a PARTIAL PLAN row. The reason was one grey row at the BOTTOM of the action list — "pokemon-mono seed check unavailable · Ability "Flame Body" is not legal for Ponyta". Ponyta in this fork's calc data has exactly one ability, Flame Body (R&B changed it); vendor/pokemon-run-runtime lists Ponyta as {abilities:["Run Away"]}, which is vanilla. Every one of the 1,039 species in the vendored table has exactly one ability, so this is a whole-table generation difference, not a stray row. Measured across the profile oracle's wild tables: 472 wild species, 36 absent from the provider entirely, and 97 of the remaining 436 carry an R&B ability the provider rejects. Bunnelby and Buneary are both on Route 101, so a nuzlocke can trip it on its first catch — three of three scripted playthroughs did. lib/pokemon-bridge.js:55 sends only run.party, so the failure lasts exactly as long as that Pokemon is in the party, and client.planBatch fails the WHOLE batch, so all three forecast fights are lost together. The degradation is near-silent: renderPlanOutlook(null) sets hidden on the outlook block and the is-top provider row is never prepended, so the panel looks like a plan that simply has no forecast. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, 2026-08-25, across all 170 reports in ui-playthrough-out: this does not degrade the forecast, it ends it. 170 of 170 runs lose the fair-dice forecast — 100% — and the median run loses it on its FIRST fight. 1,532 of the 1,708 problems ever logged by the driver are this one thing, which is 90% of everything it has ever complained about. That follows from the 22% rather than contradicting it. A box of 22 wild catches has about a 0.4% chance of containing no refused species at all (0.78^22), so a run that keeps its forecast is the rare case and none of the 170 hit it. 51 distinct species were refused in practice. The most frequent: Flame Body on Ponyta (151 times), Keen Eye on Fletchling (136), Keen Eye on Staravia (123), Keen Eye on Fletchinder (112), Swift Swim on Seadra (111), Cute Charm on Phanpy (111), Flame Body on Sizzlipede (95), Reckless on Rhyhorn (81). This is why plan-verdict-hides-a-dead-forecast mattered so much: the verdict was hiding a forecast that is dead in every run rather than an occasional one. 70621cd made that visible, and the visibility fix is doing work on every fight of every run. It does not fix this. The survival answer is still absent everywhere. LAYERING, traced 2026-08-25. The divergence is not unrecorded — it is recorded and then not consulted. vendor/pokemon-run-runtime/DATA-DIVERGENCES.json holds all 124 ability divergences species by species, naming both sides ({"species":"Aron","field":"abilities", "vendor":["Sturdy"],"fork":["Heavy Metal"]}), across 1,244 species compared, and tests/provider-data.test.js fails on any drift from it. Only that test and scripts/diff-provider-data.js read the file. Nothing at the call site does. The call site is src/js/pokemon_provider_client.js line 84, which serialises `ability: mon.ability || undefined` — the FORK ability, straight from the run document. The provider then checks it against its own table (createPlayerPokemon: if the species ability list does not include the supplied ability, throw). So layer 3 declares the contract and layer 4 breaks it. And the declared failure mode is not the real one. Both the ledger meaning and the header of scripts/diff-provider-data.js say a receipt for a diverging species is COMPUTED FROM THE VENDOR VALUES — wrong numbers, silently. That holds for the 16 baseStats divergences, where nothing is passed in to check. It does not hold for the 124 ability divergences, where the ability IS passed in and validated: those do not compute from wrong numbers, they throw, and the receipt never exists. The documented behaviour is degradation and the actual behaviour is absence. CORRECTION to the consequence recorded above: I wrote that the forecast dies "for the rest of the run". That phrase is the driver's own log wording and forecastReported is only a dedupe set, so the message asserts a permanence it does not measure. Measured properly across 169 runs with three or more planned fights: 95 (56%) lose the forecast in EVERY planned fight, and 74 (44%) lose it in some and keep it in others. The median run has no forecast in 100% of its fights. Severe, and not the same claim. The retirement path the design names — curate mono's species table to R&B values and re-pin — cannot be done from this repository: vendor/pokemon-run-runtime holds only a bundled index.js, PROVENANCE.json and package.json, with no species source to curate. ATTRIBUTION CORRECTED, 2026-08-25. The consequence recorded above blamed this finding for the whole of the forecast collapse, and 37% of it was ours. Splitting the 2,610 recorded rejections by whether the species is an evolution of something: 974 across 32 evolved forms were the run carrying a pre-evolution ability across evolution — Swift Swim on Seadra is Horsea's, Keen Eye on Fletchinder is Fletchling's — which is a defect in lib/run.js, not in the provider table, and is fixed in 26dfbc0. 1,636 across 19 base forms are this finding: Aron, Buneary, Bunnelby, Croagunk, Fletchling, Krabby, Ledyba, Litleo, Mudbray, Phanpy, Ponyta, Qwilfish, Rhyhorn, Rookidee, Sizzlipede, Skitty, Staryu, Torkoal, Yanma. So "51 distinct species were refused" was a true count of a mixed set; 19 of them belong here. MEASURED AFTER 26dfbc0, six fresh runs: the share of planned fights that keep a live forecast rose from 2.9% (114 of 3,952) to 14.5% (24 of 165), and no evolved form appears among the remaining ability rejections — only base forms, which is what this finding predicts. So "the survival answer is still absent everywhere" is no longer accurate either: it is absent in 85.5% of fights, and the largest single cause of what remains is not abilities at all but trainer-name resolution, 77 of 101 failures. PRACTICAL SURFACE, measured 2026-08-25 after the other three causes were cleared. With the stale-ability-on-evolution bug fixed, the trainer resolver shipped and planBatch failing per fight, the forecast runs at 19.8% of planned fights (33 of 167 across six runs) and EVERY remaining failure is this finding. Trainer failures are zero. The surface is far smaller than the 124 divergences suggest. Ten (species, ability) pairs account for all 134 remaining failures: Litleo/Unnerve 30, Ponyta/Flame Body 22, Rhyhorn/Reckless 18, Phanpy/Cute Charm 17, Sizzlipede/Flame Body 15, Croagunk/Poison Touch 12, Steenee/Sweet Veil 9, Luxio/Intimidate 8, Ledyba/Rattled 2, Rookidee/Unnerve 1. They are the species a Nuzlocke catches on the early routes, which is why they dominate. Curating those ten would take the forecast from 19.8% to essentially 100%. Probing what the engine WILL accept confirms the diagnosis exactly: it wants the vanilla ability in every case — Litleo Rivalry, Ponyta Run Away, Rhyhorn Lightning Rod, Phanpy Pickup, Sizzlipede Flash Fire, Croagunk Anticipation, Steenee Leaf Guard, Luxio Rivalry, Rookidee Keen Eye. One observation that bears on how it could be fixed, and is NOT a recommendation. The ability the engine builds is an object, not a name, and its effects array is EMPTY even for an ability it accepts: Magmar with a legal Flame Body comes back {name:"Flame Body", description:"RAB Gen 8 ability with RAB modifications", effects:[]}, identical in shape to Run Away. So within this bundle the species-to-ability table is acting as a legality gate rather than as the source of behaviour. Whether the engine consults it again during planning cannot be established from outside the bundle, and assuming it does not would be exactly the reasoning-instead-of-measuring this work has been caught by twice. So the options are: curate the ten upstream and re-pin, which is correct and needs a source this repository does not have; or override createPlayerPokemon at the factory to bypass the check, which is reaching into a pinned artifact's contract and is Philip's call rather than mine. Sending the vendor's vanilla ability instead remains ruled out on measurement: six of six substitutions changed incoming damage in most cells, and Intimidate against Rivalry moved five of six. MEASURED 2026-08-25 against both pinned sides. 124 of 1,244 comparable species share NO ability between the fork and the engine, and it bites where a nuzlocke shops: 34 of the 134 species these logs record catching are contradicted, covering 2,212 of 9,089 catches (24.3%). Croagunk, Ponyta, Phanpy, Fletchling and Bunnelby are all early-route staples and all refused, and one refused party member kills the forecast for every fight while it is in the box — which is the whole of the 19.8% forecast rate. There is nothing to reconcile: profiles/run-and-bun/index.js marks data.ABILITY_SLOT_CHANGES source-of-truth, verified against github.com/dekzeh/runandbundex species/base_stats.h and gated by tests/runbun_species.test.js, while the engine ships vanilla. The fork is right. Forcing the engine answer would restore all 124 forecasts and make 72 of them WRONG — Aron Heavy Metal becomes Sturdy, which survives any hit from full HP — so it is not done: a guess is worse than a gap. No injection point exists either, since createPlayerPokemon is installed after the caller options are spread and the species table is closure-scoped. The fix is one table, upstream: rebuild the vendored artifact from a pokemon-mono build carrying Run and Bun abilities. profiles/run-and-bun/oracle/ability-reconciliation.json is the exact diff that work needs, generated by scripts/build-ability-reconciliation.js and gated by tests/ability_reconciliation.test.js. FIXED 2026-08-25 at the source rather than bridged around. The upstream table rab-gen8-pokemon-complete.ts says "Extracted from RunBunCalc species.ts" and did not match that source; regenerating its abilities from the fork data takes contradicted species 124 -> 0. An unmodified rebuild of the old pin reproduced the vendored artifact byte for byte (sha256 5503927e...), so the new bundle differs only by that correction. Measured after: 78 of 78 planned fights across three runs carry a live survival forecast, against 19.8% before, and zero ability refusals. The provider diff falls from 140 divergences across 132 species to 14 across 7, all base stats on species that are generation drift rather than Run & Bun changes.

findings.claim: resolveRabTrainerOrder throws for 152 of the 362 fights in this profile's run map (42%). The two sides name the same fights differently — doubles, numbered duplicate grunts and rival variants — so the pinned provider cannot be asked about most of the run.
findings.evidence: Measured: for every trainer in planner.listFights('run-and-bun'), call vendor resolveRabTrainerOrder. 152 of 362 throw "No unique canonical RAB trainer exists". The failures are a naming convention, not missing content: "Team Aqua Grunt Museum #1/#2" (our disambiguating suffix), "Twins Gina And Mia" and "School Kid Jerry & Johnson" (doubles written as one label), and "Trainer Rival Cycling Road Sceptile" (our rival-variant pattern). Singles with plain names resolve fine — Youngster Calvin 3, Lady Cindy 9, Leader Brawly 28, Leader Roxanne 46. Seen in play as "pokemon-mono seed check unavailable · No unique canonical RAB trainer exists for "Team Aqua Grunt Petalburg Woods"" while the player was standing in front of Lady Cindy, because run_panel.js planningFights forecasts the next THREE fights as one batch. FIXED in 69be9e4. This finding had the diagnosis right on 2026-08-21 — "a naming convention, not missing content", naming the doubles, the numbered grunts and the rival variants — and the fix follows straight from it. The engine files a double under its lead and records the other half, so "School Kid Jerry & Johnson" is its "School Kid Jerry" with the same four Pokemon. The TEAM is therefore a key both transcriptions share, and matching on it places 124 of the 152 uniquely and none ambiguously. 210 of 362 resolved before (58.0%), 334 after (92.3%), measured through the shipped browser bundle. Safe because it is checkable: on the 210 the engine already resolves by name, team matching agrees 191 times and disagrees never. The 28 that remain are the part this finding did NOT cover, and they are genuinely missing content rather than naming: Leader Flannery, Bug Maniac James, Breeder Lydia, Breeder Corgi, Breeder Isaac and Ranger Lydian have no counterpart in the engine at all, and Bird Keeper Perry & Chester is four Pokemon here against eight there. They are refused rather than guessed, because an order off by one names a different trainer's team.

findings.claim: The Plan verdict never says whether you survive. Its fair-dice forecast — the only part that does — is dead for most of the game, and when it dies the verdict does not say so. Meanwhile the survival answer EXISTS, is accurate, and is in a different panel behind a different button.
findings.evidence: Eight scripted playthroughs (scripts/ui-playthrough.js), eight different parties, all eight lost the forecast and all eight died at Lady Cindy. Before that fight the verdict read "Lady Cindy — contested by 0.1. Plan for both." and the only sign of trouble was the LAST row of the action list, in the same grey as an unavailable option: "— pokemon-mono seed check unavailable · No unique canonical RAB trainer exists for Team Aqua Grunt Petalburg Woods" — a different trainer two fights away. renderPlanOutlook(null) then sets hidden on the whole outlook block and the is-top PARTIAL PLAN row is never prepended, so a dead forecast is indistinguishable from a plan that never had one. Compare a working forecast, which is unmissable: "0 of 8 fair-dice samples came back clean · worst sampled branch loses 1". Two causes feed it, both recorded separately: [[provider-ability-table-is-vanilla-not-run-and-bun]] and [[provider-cannot-resolve-42-percent-of-the-run-map]]. The batch makes it worse — client.planBatch covers the next three fights and fails as a unit, so an unresolvable trainer two steps ahead removes the forecast for the fight in front of you. MEASURED, and this is the part that decides the severity: across twelve scripted playthroughs the Best-parties adjudication called every single outcome. 25 fights were played by the six that Rank scored. The 22 it scored at or above 9/12 clean were ALL won (mean 99% of sims clean, 0.6 deaths avg); the 3 it scored below were ALL wiped (mean 44% clean, 3.7 deaths avg), and two of those named the exact Pokemon nothing on the team answered — "won 5/12 sims · 3.0 deaths avg · unanswered: Jigglypuff" before Lady Cindy, "won 4/12 sims · 4.7 deaths avg · unanswered: Yanma" before Triathlete Mikey. Both wiped. The Plan verdict for those same two fights read "contested by 0.1. Plan for both." and "contested by 1.4. Plan for both." So the tool is not failing to know — it knows, accurately, and puts it behind Rank parties rather than in the verdict the player reads next to the Fight button. MEASURED 2026-08-24, nine encounters-mode playthroughs, 376 distinct first attempts (retries excluded, because a boss retried twenty times floods any band it sits in): the verdict does not track the outcome, because it was never a forecast. planner.js:468 sets margin to top.score minus runnerUp.score — the gap between OUR best action and OUR second best, which measures how obvious the move choice is. Win rate by band: decided 5.0+ 84.2% (n=190), decided 2.0-5.0 96.1% (n=51), contested 1.0-2.0 97.2% (n=36), contested <0.5 93.0% (n=86), contested 0.5-1.0 84.6% (n=13). The most emphatic band is the WORST performing one. A reader who takes "decided by 6.4" as "this fight is decided" is reading a sentence the number cannot support: Trainer Chelle Daycare reads "contested by 0.15" and went 0 for 12. PARTLY ADDRESSED in 70621cd, and deliberately left open. The claim has two halves. "When it dies the verdict does not say so" is fixed: the notice moved from the last row of the action list, where it carried a class with no styling in main.css and read as one more unavailable move, to the top slot the working forecast occupies, styled on the warn tokens and leading with "NO SURVIVAL CHECK · nothing here says whether you live through this fight". The other half is untouched: the Plan verdict still never answers survival even when the forecast is healthy, and the answer still lives in a different panel behind a different button. Whether Plan should carry it is a product decision, so it is Philip's.

findings.claim: The held-item picker offers every item in the bag, and give accepts any of them. Hand a Pokemon a Potion and the run cannot plan or fight until someone works out which Pokemon is holding what and takes it back.
findings.evidence: Reproduced by scripts/ui-playthrough.js playing the panel as offered: it picked the first bag item out of #runbun-run-hold-item and pressed Give. Starly took a Potion, and the next two calls both failed 400 — /run/plan and /run/battle/start — with "Starly (player-3) holds "Potion", which is not an item this game can hold in battle — fix or take the item" (lib/planner.js:180). The run made no further progress. The rule is already written and exported: planner.holdableItem (lib/planner.js:693). lib/run.js:1376 uses it to filter the advisor's give options under a comment that names this exact hazard — "Most of a bag is not a held item — Rare Candy, Heart Scales, repels — and handing one to the calculator is a refusal, not a build." Neither the give command (lib/run.js:2764) nor the picker consults it, and the picker's own comment claims it offers "the bag's holdable items" while filtering only on count > 0. FIXED in two independent halves, each falsified on its own. The server is the authority: `give` now calls planner.holdableItem and refuses by name — "give: Potion is not an item a Pokemon can hold — it stays in the bag" — so the refusal arrives at the action that caused it, naming the item, instead of two actions later from playerStateFromEntry naming a battle slot. The picker is convenience: it filters the bag through the same Gen 8 item table, reached the way speciesTypes already reaches species data, and says "Nothing in the bag can be held" rather than the false "The bag is empty". An absent calc means offer everything — hiding the whole bag because reference data has not loaded is worse than an item the server declines with a reason. Gated at both layers: tests/run.test.js refuses Potion, Rare Candy, Heart Scale and Escape Rope and checks the bag is untouched by the refusal; tests/browser_run.test.js reaches the point where the bag holds exactly one Potion and asserts the picker offers nothing, then acquires an Oran Berry and asserts it offers exactly that. Falsified separately — removing the server guard reddens run.test.js, removing the picker filter reddens browser_run.test.js. Confirmed in the live UI: a bag of Potion, Rare Candy, Heart Scale and Oran Berry offers only the berry, and a hand-posted give of the Potion returns 400 with the save byte-identical.

findings.claim: renderBox builds the PC list from the COMMITTED party while the strip renders the STAGED one, so a member removed from the strip belongs to neither list. It disappears from the screen with no control anywhere to bring it back.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in the browser on a run whose only Pokemon was its starter. Before: strip [mon-1], PC list "Every living Pokemon is in the party.", zero add buttons. Clicked the strip's x. After: strip empty, PC list STILL "Every living Pokemon is in the party.", still zero add buttons — two statements on screen at once that contradict each other, and Piplup on neither list. reserve = alive.filter(mon => state.party.indexOf(mon.id) === -1) at line 796 is the cause: staging is not consulted. The only exits are committing the party you did not want (an empty party is legal and returns the summary "the party is empty") or reloading, which re-syncs stagedParty from state.party. It matters because acting on the Rank answer means restaging, and Rank names a six with a lead — see [[rank-answer-is-not-a-control]].

findings.claim: Best parties ranks every legal six and renders them as plain list rows. There is no way to press the winner — the player has to read the species names off the row and rebuild that party by hand, in that order, through a staging flow that hides anything it drops.
findings.evidence: renderRanking builds each row as li.runbun-run-rank-row holding spans only, and the block in src/index.template.html:2704 is a bare <ol> with no action. Rows carry no data-id either, so even a script has to match the six back to the box by species name. The rows are worth acting on — a real one from a playthrough reads "2.885 Piplup Starly Natu Steenee [Surskit] Ponyta won 12/12 sims · 0.1 deaths avg", lead in brackets. The project already fixed this shape once elsewhere: the browser gate has a test called "the worst-case cell is a control, and pressing it actually answers".

findings.claim: RAISED AND WRONG. Claimed Attract must check gender. In Run & Bun it must not: gender-independent Attract is a declared source-of-truth profile mechanic, and an audit had already closed this exact question.
findings.evidence:
Kept as a record of a wrong call, not a defect. The observation was real — Attract lands on same-gender targets, 9 times across four playthroughs — but the conclusion was backwards, and four places in this repository say so:
  - profiles/run-and-bun/index.js:108 sets mechanics.attractIsGenderIndependent: true, and :194 tags it "source-of-truth", the highest provenance tier the profile has.
  - docs/AI_DATA_MODEL.md:538 — "Run & Bun Attract is intentionally gender-independent, so same-gender and genderless targets still pass the ordinary volatile-immunity and ability-protection checks."
  - docs/AI_DATA_MODEL.md:620 — "Attract respects target ability protection without gender gating."
  - docs/INVENTORY.md, audit soul-dew-and-infatuation-verified (2026-08-12) — "Attract has no gender gate. Both were already implemented and pinned; the audit closed the question rather than changing code."
The two fixtures I flipped were not a bug locked in by omission; they were the rule, asserted on purpose. The fix add7f3a is reverted in dedb4d0. What should have happened: read the profile mechanics and the battle docs before treating a deviation from mainline as a defect — a hack IS its deviations, and this one is flagged, sourced and audited. Leaves one real question behind, [[cute-charm-gender-gate-undecided]].

findings.claim: Every Pokemon with a gender is built male, including female-only species. Nothing in the run carries gender at all: rollIdentity does not roll one and partySpecs does not pass one, so the engine never sees a real one.
findings.evidence: Built one fight state per species through planner.buildFightState and read the gender back. Piplup M, Jigglypuff M, Miltank M, Nidoran-F M — the last two are female-ONLY species. Magnemite and Ditto correctly come back undefined, so the genderless case is handled and the gendered case is not: it is defaulted, not derived. rollIdentity (lib/run.js:133) authors the rolled identity — six IVs, a nature and an ability — and does not author a gender; partySpecs (lib/run.js:1084) forwards species, level, nature, ability, item, moves and IVs, and does not forward one. The M itself is invented in the vendored calculator, calc/src/pokemon.ts:66, `options.gender || this.species.gender || 'M'` — a form default a web user overrides and a headless run never does. DOWNGRADED high->low on 2026-08-26 after pricing it, which the original entry did not do. Gender has no consumer this run can reach. Infatuation is gender-independent by declared source-of-truth rule, which accounts for Attract and for Cute Charm — the engine's Cute Charm path (ai/src/move-engine.ts:4740) checks no gender itself and defers to canApplyVolatile, inheriting that ruling — so [[attract-and-cute-charm-ignore-gender]] is refuted, not supporting evidence. That leaves Rivalry (calc/src/mechanics/gen789.ts:1028) and Captivate. Scanned all 1624 enemy Pokemon across 362 fights by ability and move name: zero Rivalry, zero Captivate. Of the twelve dex species carrying a gender-reading ability only Phanpy, Buneary and Lopunny are catchable, and all three are Cute Charm. So the fabricated gender is currently inert in both directions. It is also underivable: no gender ratio exists anywhere in the data — the calc species exposes only kind, id, name, baseStats, types, weightkg, abilities, plus gender N for genderless — so a fix means authoring a new sourced table, not reading one. Left open rather than wontfix because that table could arrive. Guarded meanwhile by a tripwire in tests/runbun_mechanics.test.js that fails the day content adds a Rivalry holder or a Captivate user, since either would be priced against a fabrication: Rivalry would read same-gender and take its 1.25x unconditionally, Captivate would never fire.

findings.claim: Best upgrades for the next fight drops any TM or tutor move whose unlock timing is unknown, and that is most of them. The panel says so in its own note — 9 upgrades compared against 60 moves skipped at the first fight — so the strongest advice surface in the tool runs on roughly a tenth of what a party can learn.
findings.evidence: Read straight off #runbun-run-advice-note during a scripted playthrough, four fights sampled: Youngster Calvin (#0) 9 compared / 60 skipped; Fisherman Darian (#14) 9 / 50; Lady Cindy (#16) 3 / 45; Team Aqua Grunt Petalburg Woods (#19) 2 / 36. lib/run.js:1349 is the drop — a teachable route with a null gate from oracle.moveObtainableAt is excluded and counted, which is the right call (offering a move the player cannot yet get is worse than silence) and is why the number is visible at all. The data is partly there: oracle.moveAvailability() returns 78 dated sources, 50 TM and 28 tutor, with zero undated among them. So the table is not missing, it is small relative to the learnsets it is asked about. The consequence shows in play: the advisor mostly offers held items and level-up moves, and the upgrades it did find were worth +0.74, +0.17 and +0.07 damage. Settling this is Philip's open question tm-tutor-dates in DECISIONS.json, which already names the community Item Locations doc as the import; this finding only measures what it is costing. DIAGNOSED 2026-08-25, and it is smaller and more fixable than "a tenth of the movepool" suggests. The skip is not the filter being crude. lib/run.js:1376 drops a teachable move when oracle.moveObtainableAt returns null, and for a six-strong party at level 24 that is 15 moves. Every one of those 15 is in the profile's own TM and tutor table — none is a move Run & Bun does not hand out. What they lack is a DATE: the table holds 78 entries and 22 of them carry opensAt: null, so the run knows the move exists and not when. 11 of those 22 name a place the map table already dates, once the two spellings are reconciled — the moves say "Route 111" and the maps say "Route111", which is why a first pass found only 7. Of the 11, 8 are a plain field item or an NPC on a dated map and 3 are gated on something the map does not answer: Dual Wingbeat needs the Mach Bike, Flash Cannon a Meteorite to trade, Fly a rival beaten.
